input: time is an integer in [0,1000000000]. clips contains n closed intervals [start,end] with 0 <= start <= end <= 1000000000, in arbitrary order. Clips may be trimmed when covering the target. All collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections. Node fields, where present, are ordinary data fields. Every individual collection length and computed allocation dimension/count fits [0,4294967295]; explicitly stated padded sizes and heap child-index arithmetic must also fit the declared exact numeric domain. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is permitted. Preconditions are not runtime-checked; allocation/resource capacity and actual completion still require qualification. JavaScript integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Number, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt; separately declared probabilities are finite primitive Number.
return: Minimum number of clips whose union covers [0,time], or -1 when impossible. For time zero, returns zero without selecting a clip.
mutation_aliasing: Copies the outer clips array before sorting; caller order and every clip row remain unchanged. No mutable aliases are returned. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Endpoint comparator differences remain exact in [-1000000000,1000000000]. Coverage coordinates are endpoints and selected count at most n. All integer inputs and integer intermediates (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain in [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(n log(n + 1) + 1) time under a comparison sort and O(n + 1) auxiliary copied-array/sort storage. One forward scan consumes each clip once; every greedy step takes the furthest reach among clips starting at or before current coverage. Bounds count ordinary built-in allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop, and stated hash/sort guarantees where relevant.
